title: Out of memory killed: dotnet 12×, rootlesskit 8×, buildkitd 6×, containerd 4×, containerd-star 4×, containerd-root 3×, (containerd-ro 2×, realpath 2×, (sd-pam 1×, 9 1×, dbus-daemon 1×, exe 1×, grep 1×, systemd 1× (7 days)
fix: Add memory or swap (Prevent tab), or limit that service with MemoryMax=
about: The system ran out of memory and stopped a program to keep itself running. That program may have been your website, your database or a job halfway through.
risk: It will happen again at the next busy moment, and the program that is stopped may not come back by itself.
steps: See which program was stopped: it is named above.
Give the server more memory, or add a swap file (the Prevent screen can add one).
If one program keeps growing, put a memory limit on it (MemoryMax= in its service).

title: demo-fail.service has failed: demo-fail.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
about: A service is a program the server keeps running in the background, such as a website or a database. This one has stopped with an error.
risk: Whatever it does, such as serving a site or running jobs, isn't happening until it runs again.
steps: Read its last lines of log to see why it stopped.
Fix what the log points at, such as a wrong setting or a full disk.
Then restart it, and check it stays running.

title: Backups are on the system disk: a disk failure loses both
about: The backups sit on the same disk as the data they protect.
risk: If that disk breaks, the data and its backups are lost together.
steps: Copy the backups to another machine or to cloud storage.
Or point the backup tool at a place off this server.

title: No swap: one memory spike kills a process
fix: Prevent tab can add a swap file
about: Swap is room on the disk the system can borrow when memory runs out. This server has none, so there is no cushion at all.
risk: One sudden spike in memory use makes the system stop a program at once.
steps: Add a swap file: the Prevent screen does it in one step.
A swap file of 1 to 2 GB is enough for most small servers.

title: No firewall is active
fix: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw enable (allow SSH first). A cloud firewall counts too
about: A firewall decides which connections from the internet may reach this server. None is switched on here.
risk: Any program that opens a port, even by mistake, can be reached by anyone.
steps: Allow SSH first, so you don't lock yourself out.
Then switch the firewall on: the command is above.
A firewall at your cloud provider counts too, if you use one.

title: Nothing blocks repeated SSH guesses
fix: sudo apt-get install fail2ban, then sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban
about: Nothing slows down people who keep guessing SSH passwords. A tool like fail2ban blocks an address after a few wrong tries.
risk: Guessing can go on day and night until a password is found.
steps: Install fail2ban and switch it on: the command is above.
Better still, log in with keys only, so there is no password to guess.

title: 66 updates waiting
about: Newer versions of installed software are waiting. None is marked as a security fix, so this is less urgent.
risk: Bugs that are already fixed stay, and the longer updates wait the bigger the next jump is.
steps: Install them at a quiet time: ByteSweep shows exactly what it will run first.
If the system then says a restart is needed, restart when it suits you.

title: A reboot is waiting: installed fixes aren't active yet
about: Updates were installed that only take effect after a restart. Until then the old, unfixed versions are still running.
risk: The holes the updates close stay open until the machine restarts.
steps: Pick a quiet time, when few people use it.
Restart it: ByteSweep shows what it will do first, and bsweep reboot --at picks a time instead.
Check your sites and services are running again afterwards.

title: The clock is kept right by chronyc
about: The clock is kept in step with a time server.

title: Names resolve
